items.content: Create an isolated Python environment: `python -m venv .venv`, then activate it before installing packages.

items.title: cargo

items.title: go run / go build
items.content: Compile and run Go code: `go run main.go`; build a binary with `go build`.

items.title: make
items.content: Run tasks defined in a Makefile: `make build`, `make test`—a language-agnostic task runner.

items.title: curl vs wget
items.content: `curl` transfers data and is great for APIs; `wget` is best for downloading files recursively.

items.title: HTTP Methods
items.content: GET reads, POST creates, PUT replaces, PATCH partially updates, DELETE removes—the REST verb set.

items.title: HTTP Status 401 vs 403
items.content: 401 means not authenticated (who are you?); 403 means authenticated but not allowed (you can't).

items.title: Conventional Commits
items.content: Commit message convention (feat:, fix:, chore:) that enables automated changelogs and versioning.

items.title: Git Flow vs Trunk-Based
items.content: Git Flow uses long-lived branches and releases; trunk-based keeps short branches merged often to main.

items.title: README Best Practices
items.content: A good README covers what, why, install, usage, configuration, contributing, and license.

items.title: Code Review Checklist
items.content: Check correctness, readability, tests, security, performance, and naming before approving a PR.

items.title: Cron Syntax
items.content: Five fields—minute, hour, day-of-month, month, day-of-week—schedule recurring jobs (e.g. `0 2 * * *`).

items.title: Regex Cheat Sheet
items.content: `\d` digit, `\w` word char, `+` one-or-more, `*` zero-or-more, `^`/`$` anchors, `[]` set, `()` group.

items.title: Semantic Versioning (ref)
items.content: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH—break.feature.fix; pre-release tags like -beta.1 and build metadata with +.

items.title: Common HTTP Headers
items.content: Content-Type, Authorization, Cache-Control, Accept, User-Agent, and CORS headers shape requests and responses.

items.title: Markdown Basics
items.content: `#` headings, `*italic*`, `**bold**`, `- lists`, `[text](url)` links, and ``` code blocks.

items.title: Time Complexity Cheat Sheet
items.content: Array access O(1), search O(n), sorted search O(log n), good sorts O(n log n), nested loops O(n^2).

items.title: Glossary: Idempotent vs Nullipotent
items.content: Idempotent operations are safe to repeat; nullipotent (like GET) also have no side effects at all.

items.title: Status Code Quick Map
items.content: 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 301/302 redirect, 400/401/403/404, 429 too many, 500/503 server.

items.title: Database Index Rules of Thumb
items.content: Index columns in WHERE/JOIN/ORDER BY, prefer selective columns, avoid over-indexing, and watch write cost.

items.title: Webhook vs Polling
items.content: Webhooks push events to you the moment they happen; polling repeatedly asks—webhooks are efficient, polling is simple.

items.title: Throughput Bottleneck
items.content: The single slowest stage that caps overall system throughput; find and widen it before scaling elsewhere.

items.title: Graceful Shutdown
items.content: Stop taking new work, finish in-flight requests, flush buffers, and close connections to avoid data loss.

items.title: Bulkhead Pattern
items.content: Isolate resources into pools so a failure in one area can't drain capacity from the rest of the system.

items.title: Strangler Fig Pattern
items.content: Incrementally replace a legacy system by routing pieces of functionality to a new one until the old is gone.

items.title: Sidecar Pattern
items.content: Deploy a helper container alongside the main one to add logging, proxying, or security without changing it.

items.title: Feature Toggle Types
items.content: Release, experiment, ops, and permission toggles each control different aspects of behavior at runtime.

items.title: Cache Stampede
items.content: When many requests miss the cache at once and overwhelm the backend; prevent with locks or staggered TTLs.

items.title: Hot vs Cold Storage
items.content: Hot storage is fast and costly for active data; cold storage is cheap and slow for archives.

items.title: Eventual vs Strong Consistency
items.content: Strong consistency returns the latest write everywhere immediately; eventual converges over time for higher availability.

items.title: Idempotent HTTP Methods
items.content: GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent—repeating them has the same effect; POST is not.

items.title: Schema Evolution
items.content: Evolve data formats (add optional fields, avoid renames) so old and new code interoperate safely.

items.title: Dependency Inversion
items.content: Depend on abstractions, not concretions, so high-level modules aren't tied to low-level details.

items.title: Law of Demeter
items.content: Talk only to your immediate collaborators—don't reach through objects—to reduce coupling.

items.title: Composition over Inheritance
items.content: Build behavior by combining small components rather than deep class hierarchies that are rigid.

items.title: Cache busting on deploy
items.content: Fingerprint asset filenames (app.abc123.js) so users always fetch the new version after a release.

items.title: Use database constraints
items.content: Enforce uniqueness, foreign keys, and not-null at the DB level—app checks alone will eventually be bypassed.

items.title: Prefer allow-lists over deny-lists
items.content: Define what's permitted rather than trying to enumerate everything dangerous—safer by default.

items.title: Keep PRs small
items.content: Small pull requests get reviewed faster, more thoroughly, and are easier to revert if something breaks.

items.title: Write deterministic tests
items.content: Avoid real time, randomness, and network in tests; inject them so runs are repeatable and reliable.

items.title: Set up pre-commit hooks
items.content: Run lint, format, and quick tests before each commit to catch issues before they reach CI.

items.title: Monitor what users feel
items.content: Track real user latency and error rates (RUM), not just server metrics, to see the actual experience.

items.title: Plan capacity ahead
items.content: Estimate growth and load-test before launches so you scale proactively instead of firefighting outages.

items.title: Document API errors
items.content: List every error code, its meaning, and how to recover so integrators aren't left guessing.

items.title: Avoid global mutable state
items.content: Shared mutable globals cause hidden coupling and race conditions; pass state explicitly instead.

items.title: Bubble Sort
items.content: Repeatedly swaps adjacent out-of-order elements so large values 'bubble' to the end. Simple but slow at O(n^2).

items.title: Selection Sort
items.content: Repeatedly selects the smallest remaining element and places it in order. O(n^2), minimal swaps.

items.title: Insertion Sort
items.content: Builds the sorted list one item at a time by inserting each into its correct place. O(n^2) but fast on nearly-sorted data.

items.title: Merge Sort
items.content: Divide-and-conquer sort that splits, recursively sorts, then merges. Stable, guaranteed O(n log n).

items.title: Quick Sort
items.content: Divide-and-conquer sort that partitions around a pivot. Average O(n log n), worst O(n^2); usually fastest in practice.

items.title: Radix Sort
items.content: Non-comparison sort that orders numbers digit by digit using counting. O(nk) for k-digit keys.

items.title: Heap Sort
items.content: Builds a max-heap then repeatedly extracts the max to sort in place. O(n log n), not stable.

items.title: Counting Sort
items.content: Counts occurrences of each value to place them in order. O(n+k), great for small integer ranges.

items.title: Linear Search
items.content: Scans each element until the target is found. O(n); works on unsorted data.

items.title: Binary Search (algo)
items.content: Repeatedly halves a sorted range to find a target in O(log n). Requires sorted input.

items.title: Two Pointers
items.content: Use two indices moving toward each other or in tandem to solve array/string problems in O(n).

items.title: Sliding Window
items.content: Maintain a moving subrange to compute running results (max sum, longest substring) efficiently in O(n).

items.title: Recursion (algo)
items.content: A function that calls itself on smaller inputs until a base case; underpins divide-and-conquer and tree/graph traversal.

items.title: Backtracking
items.content: Explore candidates incrementally and abandon ('backtrack') ones that can't lead to a solution—used for puzzles, permutations, N-Queens.

items.title: Divide and Conquer
items.content: Break a problem into independent subproblems, solve recursively, and combine—basis of merge sort and binary search.

items.title: Frequency Counter Pattern
items.content: Use an object/map to tally values so you can compare collections in O(n) instead of nested O(n^2) loops.

items.title: Memoization (algo)
items.content: Cache results of recursive calls by their arguments to turn exponential recursion into linear time.

items.title: Breadth-First Search
items.content: Explore a graph level by level using a queue; finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs. O(V+E).

items.title: Depth-First Search
items.content: Explore a graph as deep as possible before backtracking, using recursion or a stack. O(V+E).

items.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm
items.content: Finds shortest paths from a source in a weighted graph with non-negative edges using a priority queue.

items.title: A* Search
items.content: Best-first pathfinding that adds a heuristic to Dijkstra to reach the goal faster—common in games and maps.

items.title: Bellman-Ford
items.content: Computes shortest paths allowing negative edge weights and detects negative cycles. O(V*E).

items.title: Topological Sort
items.content: Orders the nodes of a directed acyclic graph so every edge points forward—used for build/dependency ordering.

items.title: Union-Find
items.content: Disjoint-set structure with union and find (plus path compression) to track connected components efficiently.

items.title: Minimum Spanning Tree
items.content: Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms connect all nodes with minimum total edge weight.

items.title: Tree Traversal
items.content: Visit tree nodes in order: in-order, pre-order, post-order (DFS) or level-order (BFS).

items.title: Binary Search Tree Ops
items.content: Insert, search, and delete in O(log n) on a balanced BST by comparing and branching left/right.

items.title: Dynamic Programming (algo)
items.content: Solve problems by combining solutions to overlapping subproblems, stored in a table (bottom-up) or memoized (top-down).

items.title: Knapsack Problem
items.content: Classic DP problem: maximize value of items chosen under a weight limit.

items.title: Longest Common Subsequence
items.content: DP algorithm finding the longest sequence present in both inputs—used in diffs and bioinformatics.

items.title: Fibonacci (DP)
items.content: Compute Fibonacci numbers in O(n) with memoization or iteration instead of exponential naive recursion.

items.title: Greedy Algorithm (algo)
items.content: Make the locally best choice at each step (e.g. coin change, interval scheduling); fast but not always optimal.

items.title: KMP String Matching
items.content: Find a pattern in text in O(n+m) by precomputing a prefix table to skip redundant comparisons.

items.title: Hashing Algorithm
items.content: Map data to fixed-size values for fast lookups (hash tables) or integrity (SHA, MD5).

items.title: Floyd's Cycle Detection
items.content: Tortoise-and-hare technique that detects a loop in a linked list using two pointers at different speeds.

items.title: Kadane's Algorithm
items.content: Finds the maximum-sum contiguous subarray in O(n) by tracking the best sum ending at each index.

items.title: QuickSelect
items.content: Selection algorithm (like quicksort partitioning) that finds the k-th smallest element in average O(n).

items.title: Abstract Factory Pattern
items.content: Creational pattern providing an interface to create families of related objects without specifying their concrete classes.

items.title: Prototype Pattern
items.content: Creational pattern that creates new objects by cloning an existing prototype instead of instantiating from scratch.

items.title: Bridge Pattern
items.content: Structural pattern that decouples an abstraction from its implementation so the two can vary independently.

items.title: Composite Pattern
items.content: Structural pattern that lets you treat individual objects and groups of objects uniformly via a tree structure.

items.title: Flyweight Pattern
items.content: Structural pattern that shares common state between many objects to minimize memory use.

items.title: Command Pattern
items.content: Behavioral pattern that encapsulates a request as an object, enabling queuing, logging, and undo/redo.

items.title: Iterator Pattern
items.content: Behavioral pattern that provides sequential access to elements of a collection without exposing its internals.

items.title: Mediator Pattern
items.content: Behavioral pattern where a mediator object centralizes communication between components to reduce coupling.

items.title: Memento Pattern
items.content: Behavioral pattern that captures and restores an object's internal state without violating encapsulation (undo).

items.title: State Pattern
items.content: Behavioral pattern that lets an object change its behavior when its internal state changes, as if changing class.

items.title: Template Method Pattern
items.content: Behavioral pattern defining an algorithm's skeleton in a base class while subclasses fill in specific steps.

items.title: Visitor Pattern
items.content: Behavioral pattern that separates an algorithm from the object structure it operates on, adding operations without changing classes.

items.title: Chain of Responsibility Pattern
items.content: Behavioral pattern passing a request along a chain of handlers until one handles it—used in middleware.

items.title: Interpreter Pattern
items.content: Behavioral pattern that defines a grammar and an interpreter to evaluate sentences in that language.

items.title: Clean Code: Functions do one thing
items.content: Functions should be small and do exactly one thing well; if a function does several things, split it.

items.title: Clean Code: Few arguments
items.content: Prefer zero, one, or two arguments; three or more signals the function does too much or needs an object.

items.title: Clean Code: No side effects
items.content: A function should either do something or return something, not secretly change state behind the caller's back.

items.title: Clean Code: Intention-revealing names
items.content: Choose names that reveal intent and are pronounceable and searchable; a good name removes the need for a comment.

items.title: Clean Code: Comments explain why
items.content: The best comment is the one you didn't need to write; use comments for intent and warnings, not to restate code.

items.title: Clean Code: Don't comment out code
items.content: Delete dead code instead of commenting it out—version control remembers it, and stale blocks confuse readers.

items.title: Clean Code: Use exceptions, not error codes
items.content: Throw exceptions instead of returning error codes, and keep error handling separate from business logic.

items.title: Clean Code: The Boy Scout Rule
items.content: Always leave the code a little cleaner than you found it; small continuous improvements prevent decay.
